terms.gloss: a street robber, a footpad, a thug
evidence: Cic. Fat. 34: causa grassātōrī fuisse … cūr ab eō spoliārētur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: One who roams the streets at night to rob or brawl; in Cato, an idler (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Lewis & Short: “a murderer, assassin, bandit (class.)”; nocturnus, Petr. 9
terms.comment: Chiefly a murderer or assassin in Cicero and Tacitus, but Lewis & Short also gives “bandit”, and Petronius has a percussor nocturnus; grassātor is the clearer word for a street robber.

sources: Lewis & Short: grassator · Lewis & Short: percussor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 191, 195, 329.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
